newsitem.title: TAIWAN: China out of soybean/corn markets on firm prices.
newsitem.headline: China out of soybean/corn markets on firm prices.

text.p: Recent rallies in Chicago soybean and corn futures have curbed China's buying interest and Chinese buyers were expected to remain sidelined until the market corrects, mainland traders said on Monday.
"Chinese buyers are highly price-sensitive and they will not rush to buy any soybeans or corn during a rally," a China-based U.S. trader said.
"There needs to be a large correction to lure Chinese buyers back into the market now," he added.

Traders said China's buyers are concerned that buying additional soybean shipments now could put them in competition with other buyers, who have bought some U.S. soybeans for near-term delivery before the CBOT rallied.
"Buyers don't want to import any additional (soybean) shipments when they know there are other shipments that were bought at much lower prices," a trader said.
Chinese traders said U.S. weather conditions and tight supplies were the key factors for the soybean futures market.
